subject: P95/P99 validation plan and demo coordinates
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Ross <amelia.ross@nexahealth.com>, Kenji Sato <kenji.sato@nexahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-18T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: P95/P99 validation plan and demo coordinates

Hi Amelia / Kenji —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align the P95/P99 validation before the POC:

Summary from our conversation:
- Nexa target SLOs we discussed: p95 end-to-end ~< 300 ms, p99 end-to-end ~< 900 ms for interactive requests.
- Incumbent reports (inference-only) are p95 ~280 ms / p99 ~1.1 s; your client-side end-to-end telemetry averages higher (you mentioned ~400 ms / 1.5 s).
- Peak throughput target: ~150 req/s across the fleet; concurrency seen on client side ~10–15 simultaneous active sessions.
- Streaming: token-level streaming required for real-time responses; typical token interval you see is 50–80 ms.

What we need from you to run an apples-to-apples validation:
1) A short traffic profile (CSV) showing request size distribution and peak windows (example attached template).
2) 3–5 sample trace files (full request->response traces) so our instrumentation team can confirm what counts as "end-to-end" on your side.
3) Confirmation of test model(s) + prompt template to ensure parity (model family, quantized/not, any pre/post-processing).

Proposed plan / schedule:
- We run a hosted POC against a mirrored traffic profile (warm and cold runs) and capture p50/p95/p99, connection churn, and streaming inter-token latency.
- Weekly demo + sync to review artifacts. Proposed first demo: Monday 2027-06-21 at 10:00 AM PT (I can host a 45-min session including live test results).

Can you share the traces and the traffic CSV by end of day Friday (2027-06-18)? I attached a draft SLO worksheet template (v0.1) to show the metrics we’ll collect.

Thanks — looking forward to validating this tightly.

Best,
Irene Choi
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
irene@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: P95/P99 validation plan and demo coordinates

Irene — thanks for the clear recap. Attaching the worksheet we typically use (nexa-slo-worksheet-v1.xlsx) and a small set of sample traces from last week (sample_traces_20270610.json). Those traces include both streaming sessions and batch calls.

A few clarifications / answers:
- The numbers I quoted on the call were client-observed end-to-end wall clock: our front-end -> edge -> inference -> back to front-end. Incumbent vendor reports the lower inference-only numbers; the additional ~100–400 ms is network / edge / client overhead depending on region.
- For the POC please treat an "interactive request" as: ~1–3 prompts up to 256 tokens, response up to 256 tokens, streaming enabled (chunked token streaming).
- Peak observed traffic: 150 req/s overall, with bursts up to 220 req/s for ~30s during batch windows. Typical sustained concurrency per worker is 8–12.
- Streaming behaviour we care about: first-byte latency, per-token inter-arrival variance, and connection resilience (token gaps >250 ms trigger degrade).

Open items we can provide:
1) A sanitized 24-hour traffic CSV (will share by EOD Friday)
2) A small set of raw traces (attached) — note these contain internal IDs, so we included a sanitized version.
3) Confirmation on the model: we're using an LLaMA-family instance (custom fine-tune) running FP16 on the incumbent. We'll include the model manifest.

We're OK with the 6/21 10:00 AM PT slot — Kenji and I will join.

Thanks,
Amelia Ross
Sr. Engineering Manager, Nexa Health
amelia.ross@nexahealth.com

Attachments: nexa-slo-worksheet-v1.xlsx (xlsx stub); sample_traces_20270610.json (json stub)

Amelia / Kenji —

Appreciate the traces — helpful context. A few technical clarifications from the Redwood side so we measure p95/p99 in a way that maps cleanly to your telemetry:

1) Measurement boundary: are you recording client-send timestamp (JS) and final-render timestamp, or is your "end-to-end" measured at the edge? We want to align on exact events so we don't compare apples to oranges. If possible, include a single trace with exact client timestamps.

2) Connection semantics: do you use persistent connections (WS or HTTP/2) per user session, or do you open a fresh connection for each request? This affects warm vs cold start characteristics at our side.

3) Streaming chunk size: the incumbent often batches tokens into 50–200 byte chunks; can you share the typical chunkization pattern? That affects per-token latency we’ll observe.

4) Traffic shaping for tests: we propose two profiles for the POC run:
   - Interactive profile: target steady-state 100 req/s, concurrent sessions 12, 45 second bursts to 180 req/s to exercise burst behavior.
   - Batch/throughput profile: target 200 req/s sustained for 5 minutes to validate queuing and prefork behaviour.

If you can confirm the measurement boundary and connection type tonight, we’ll finalize the harness and the metric dashboards for the demo. Also, can you provide 3 representative trace IDs from the attached JSON (so we can link events)?

Irene — we’ll use the 6/21 10:00 AM PT slot for the demo and bring a short checklist: environment parity, warmup sequence, and token-stream diagnostics.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Ben / Irene —

Thanks — confirmed on the measurement boundary: we record client-send (browser) and client-receive timestamps; internal edge timestamps are available as well. I highlighted three representative trace IDs in the attached sample_traces_20270610.json (IDs: trace-20270610-137, trace-20270610-201, trace-20270610-259).

Connection model: we primarily use persistent HTTP/2 connections from the front-end to the edge; long-lived sessions are common, but we do see short-lived workers spawn during heavy batch processing.

Chunkization: typical streaming chunks are ~100–250 bytes; token batching happens aggressively on the incumbent which explains smoother token streams but higher first-byte latency.

We’ve uploaded the 24-hour sanitized traffic CSV to the Drive link below and added a HubSpot note with expected timelines. See links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C4D5E and HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/67890
